canonical_seed.student_text:
A force of 12 N east is drawn as an arrow. Which feature of the arrow should communicate the 12 N value?
A. Its length or scale.
B. Its color only.
C. The object name.
D. The page location.
canonical_seed.student_html:
A force of 12 N east is drawn as an arrow. Which feature of the arrow should communicate the 12 N value?

  1. Its length or scale.
  2. Its color only.
  3. The object name.
  4. The page location.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Vector magnitude is represented by arrow length/scale, while arrow direction represents force direction.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Vector magnitude is represented by arrow length/scale, while arrow direction represents force direction.

canonical_seed.student_text:
A sled has a net force of 35 N right. One person pulls 80 N right while another pulls left. How large is the leftward pull?
A. 35 N
B. 45 N
C. 80 N
D. 115 N

canonical_seed.solution_text: 80 N right − 45 N left = 35 N right.

canonical_seed.student_text:
Rank the three cases from greatest to least net-force magnitude.

A: 25 N ← [box] → 35 N
B: 10 N ← [box] → 45 N
C: 20 N ← [box] → 40 N
A. B > C > A
B. C > A > B
C. A > B > C
D. A = B = C

Rank the three cases from greatest to least net-force magnitude.

  2. C > A > B

canonical_seed.student_text: A rolling cart is moving left, but its force diagram has a 24 N net force to the right. What change in motion should the cart have initially? Explain.
canonical_seed.student_html: A rolling cart is moving left, but its force diagram has a 24 N net force to the right. What change in motion should the cart have initially? Explain.
canonical_seed.answer: Its velocity changes toward the right: it initially slows while moving left, because the rightward net force produces rightward acceleration.
canonical_seed.solution_text: Net force determines the direction of acceleration/change in velocity, not necessarily the current direction of motion.
canonical_seed.solution_html: Net force determines the direction of acceleration/change in velocity, not necessarily the current direction of motion.
